terms.grammar: cavē with the accusative of what to beware of
terms.comment: A description of ours, on the pattern of the sign in Petronius, CAVĒ CANEM: cavēre with the accusative is to beware of a thing, and gradus is a step of a stair. We have found no set phrase for this in the authors we searched or in Traupman.

terms.grammar: cavē nē with the present subjunctive; pedem offendere, to strike one’s foot
evidence: Ov. F. 2.720: crēditus offēnsō prōcubuisse pede
terms.comment: A sentence of ours: pedem offendere is to stub one’s foot, to trip, as Brutus pretended to do in Ovid.

phrases.english: Mind the step; give me your hand.
Careful you don’t fall; stand still.

phrases.latin: ille jacēns prōnus mātrī dedit ōscula Terrae, crēditus offēnsō prōcubuisse pede
phrases.english: lying face down, he kissed his mother Earth, and they thought he had tripped and fallen

sources: Lewis & Short: caveo · Lewis & Short: gradus · Lewis & Short: offendo
